# logflare_alert_notification_policy (Resource)

Decides which alert issue changes Logflare sends to the control plane, and for which receivers. The control plane (the platform, or Studio when self-hosted) fans each event out to the destinations behind the receiver names.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Page the ops webhook when a security advisor alert issue opens in the default project,
# and again every hour while it stays open and unacknowledged.
resource "logflare_alert_notification_policy" "advisor_pages" {
  name                    = "advisor-pages"
  rule_keys               = ["supabase.advisor.*"]
  min_severity            = "major"
  categories              = ["security"]
  identifiers             = { project = "default" }
  events                  = ["opened", "reopened", "repeat", "resolved"]
  repeat_interval_seconds = 3600
  receivers               = ["ops-webhook"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique name of the policy
- `receivers` (List of String) Receiver names the control plane maps to destinations, e.g. `ops-webhook`

### Optional

- `categories` (List of String) Categories to send: `security`, `performance`, `health`. Empty sends every category.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the policy sends events
- `events` (List of String) Changes to send: `opened`, `reopened`, `repeat`, `resolved`
- `identifiers` (Map of String) Identifiers an alert issue must have, e.g. `{ project = "default" }`
- `min_severity` (String) Lowest severity to send: `critical`, `major`, `warning` or `info`. Unset sends every severity.
- `repeat_interval_seconds` (Number) Resend open, unacknowledged alert issues this often (at least 300). Unset sends no repeats.
- `rule_keys` (List of String) Rule key globs, e.g. `supabase.advisor.*`. Empty matches every rule.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) Notification policy identifier

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Notification policies are imported by their numeric id.
terraform import logflare_alert_notification_policy.advisor_pages 1
```
